articleTitle: Developing mathematical modelling competence: conceptual clarification and educational planning
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper we introduce the concept of mathematical modelling competence, by which we mean being able to carry through a whole mathematical modelling process in a certain context. Analysing the structure of this process, six sub‐competences are identified. Mathematical modelling competence cannot be reduced to these six sub‐competences, but they are necessary elements in the development of mathematical modelling competence. Experience from the development of a modelling course is used to illustrate how the different nature of the sub‐competences can be used as a tool for finding the balance between different kinds of activities in a particular educational setting. Obstacles of social, cognitive and affective nature for the students' development of mathematical modelling competence are reported and discussed in relation to the sub‐competences.

articleTitle: Using a personal response system for promoting student interaction
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: We first descibe the introduction of an electronic feedback system in a large lecture class in Engineering Mathematics designed to promote greater student interaction. We then look at the experience of using the system where it was primarily used to support the consolidation of key concepts in tutorials in Computer Science. We discuss the issue of how the introduction of such methods turned out to be as much a learning experience for the academics involved as for the students and consider the potential of these systems.

articleTitle: Engineering students—diagnostic testing and follow up
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Improving retention rates amongst engineering students and enhancing the provision of mathematics support for all students within the University are two of the main aims of the Mathematics Learning Support Centre (MLSC; http://mlsc.lboro.ac.uk). This paper will describe some recent strategies adopted to support first year engineering students. It will also comment upon the success of these strategies.

articleTitle: Engineering mathematics—dare to hope?
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Some of the challenges encountered in the delivery of engineering mathematics courses have their origins in the changing and often non-uniform degree of mathematical preparedness of the recipients. In some cases, these challenges arise in a positive way, as a result of a deliberate policy of wider access to engineering courses. However, in others, they come about following problems encountered with mathematics provision in pre-university study, and as such are reflecting a much larger problem, one which has implications way beyond the boundaries of engineering mathematics. Mathematics at school level is plagued with enormous difficulties and uncertainties including a shortage of well-qualified teachers, and an ongoing debate on curriculum and assessment. A plethora of ``interesting'' sounding degree titles and a high demand for graduates in mathematics to enter lucrative careers, militates against the recruitment of highly-qualified teachers. Nevertheless, there are actions and initiatives aimed at supporting and strengthening school-level mathematics in various ways and this paper will describe and comment on some of them. Moreover, it aims to show that University mathematics departments/groups could play an important role in taking some of these proposals forward.

articleTitle: Section A
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper uses volleyball games to provide a few interesting examples that may be used in teaching various mathematical concepts. Suggestions for class instructions, student activities, use of computer technology, and the enhancement of problem‐solving skills are also discussed.

articleTitle: A third way of teaching mathematics to engineers
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In recognition of the need to enhance mathematics learning, particularly for under achievers, to reflect the changing pattern of student intake to undergraduate degree courses in engineering, this paper describes a proposed alternative approach, designated the third way, of teaching the mathematics component of such courses. Attributes of the third way, together with characteristics of the existing first and second ways, are discussed. Meta-level knowledge structures and learning actions of students are described and connections between these and learning mathematics are outlined.

articleTitle: Changes in student entry competencies 1991–2001
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper, data from diagnostic testing at Coventry University are used to illustrate how student entry competencies in basic mathematical skills have changed over the period 1991–2001. These data show that there has been a significant decline in many mathematical skills that are regarded by higher education as essential for those undertaking degree courses with a significant mathematical content.

articleTitle: Section A
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: At the height of the grass cutting season I saw an ingenious device being used to cut a lawn without human intervention. Naturally, this appealed to me and I thought it worthy of mathematical investigation, particularly before I put theory into practice!

articleTitle: Who is now, and who might in the future, be teaching mathematics in secondary schools?
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper reports upon aspects of work funded by the Society for Educational Studies into the supply of school mathematics and science teachers and the deployment of mathematics teachers and carried out in the Centre for Studies in Science and Mathematics Education, School of Education, University of Leeds. The last major study of the deployment of mathematics teachers was undertaken by the DES in 1977 and reported upon in the Cockcroft Report of 1982. Aspects of the present data collection were designed to be comparable to the Cockcroft data. The paper reports mainly on those aspects

articleTitle: Section A
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The provision of Further Education has increased dramatically in Ireland since the early 1990s. A small proportion of students on Post Leaving Certificate courses take Mathematics as one of their subjects of study. Mathematics in Further Education has undergone some changes over the last number of years. This article explores these changes and attempts to analyse them in the light of current thinking on mathematics curriculum provision.

articleTitle: Thoughts of higher things
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: As my year eight group were working through their exercises on calculating areas of compound shapes, one of the pupils approached me to have his work marked. After I marked his efforts he asked me if I could help him with a mathematical problem that he was working on. He then proceeded to outline the trouble he was experiencing with work on calculating the volume of a sphere in four dimensions! Not quite the sort of problem I was expecting from a year eight pupil! I had to admit to him that I was unable to help him at that moment, but that I would go away and give it some thought. This article summarizes those musings.

articleTitle: Modern mathematics for engineers and scientists
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper argues for a fundamental shift in the way mathematics is taught to engineers and scientists, away from the traditional methods approach, to an approach that makes significant use of symbolic algebra packages. The use of such packages is widely used to aid the teaching of engineering topics. This paper argues strongly in favour of the Service Mathematics community also embracing this new technology. We argue that teaching the language (comprising the notation and grammar) of mathematics will be of more use and more accessible than focusing almost entirely on teaching mathematical techniques.

articleTitle: On‐line teaching of mathematics and statistics
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Virtual Learning Environments and other online teaching tools are spreading rapidly throughout Higher Education. This article describes the results of a recent survey in their use in the teaching of Mathematics and Statistics.

articleTitle: Section B
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The common core of A‐level Mathematics includes the study of numerical methods for solution of equations. One particular syllabus requires each student to study an example of failure in the case of the Newton–Raphson method. The construction of such failures is a contrivance; yet this attempt to do so in this paper opens up a fascinating case that enlivens other aspects of the Mathematics' syllabus at that level.

articleTitle: Getting hooked on mathematics through its applications
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper, we describe a one‐day event that changed student perceptions about the relevance of mathematics in today's world. In particular, we discuss, in detail, a competition held during this event in which senior level secondary school students were given an opportunity to experience consulting in the mining industry. Many of the students found the event to be an eye‐opener, exposing them to a wealth of career opportunities that they were previously unaware of.

articleTitle: Goal‐based reform of first‐year discrete mathematics: a Swedish case study
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: We discuss a fundamental reform of the way discrete mathematics is taught at Mälardalen University. The background to this reform was a complete revision of the goals of the course, which now focus on skills rather than subject matter.

articleTitle: A MATH-KIT for engineers
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Whether we are assessing the mathematical background of incoming students or designing and assessing the mathematical modules and assessment for a given engineering programme, we need a succinct method for classifying the desired learning outcomes—a taxonomy of the learning objectives. This article describes a simple practitioner-friendly classification of educational objectives (MATH-KIT), and discusses how it can be used to design appropriate curricula, teaching methods and assessment that develop higher order learning skills in a simple and transparent way.

articleTitle: On concept images and square roots
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper discusses the consequences of the definition of a concept not standing at the core of one's image of that concept. It then zeros in on √n, and takes the position that it is not enough for students to know the definition of what √n means, but that they should also know some method which would enable them to compute √n, although carrying out the actual computation is not important. Several relatively known and unknown methods to compute √n are then discussed.

articleTitle: Six circles: almost the complete story
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: For a number of years I have run problem‐solving workshops for teachers and master classes for students. One of my most successful problems has been the Six Circle Problem. In this paper I go through the details of that problem in the hope that it may be of use either to other people involved in such workshops or to teachers in school.

articleTitle: Section B
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: A problem involving the location of centres of gravity of tumblers leads to some interesting mathematics.

articleTitle: Modelling a small internet café charging policy
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper we use a continuous time Markov chain to model a simple optimisation problem with stochastic elements. The prerequisites are a knowledge of linear constant coefficient systems and some elementary probability—including the negative exponential distribution, which is briefly reviewed. The problem addressed has wide appeal and has the advantage of being based on modelling with differential equations. It offers an alternative to the classic mechanics and population models. The problem has easy generalizations with which to create variations. Special consideration is given to looking at some of the assumptions of the model and questioning the model solution.
